title: WPMS/2408/2017 of Rohit Taneja Vs Gurdayal Kaur AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2408 of 2017
Rohit Taneja ...Petitioner

Versus
Gurdayal Kaur & Others ......Respondents
Present: Mr. Nikhil Singhal, Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the respondents
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J. (Oral)
 There was an SCC suit filed by the
respondents which was decreed on 16.04.2009 in
favour of the plaintiff-respondents. Be as it may for
whatsoever reason, the present writ petitioner invoked
provisions of Order 21 Rule 97 challenging the decree,
the application filed by the petitioner under Order 21
Rule 97 was dismissed by order dated 16.11.2015.
Since the order passed under Order 21 Rule 97 takes
the shape of a decree he took take the advantage of
the rejection and preferred an appeal which was
numbered as Appeal No. 75 of 2015.
2. During the pendency of the appeal, the
decree- holder/respondent in the appeal died on
27.12.2015. After the death of the decree holder, his
heirs moved an Application before the learned
Appellate Court, invoking Order 22 Rule 9 read with
Order 22 Rule 10-A, praying for abatement of the

2
appeal on account of failure to substitute the heirs of
the deceased decree-holder/respondent. Once it was
an appeal preferred by the petitioner and the fact of
filing of an application by the heirs of deceased decree
holder on 11.02.2016 since it was endorsed in the
order-sheet by the petitioner, it would be deemed that
the petitioner got the knowledge of the death of the
decree-holder.
3. After about almost a year i.e. on 07.02.2017
the petitioner is shown to have filed a Substitution
Application along with Delay Condonation Application,
praying for to condone the delay and to bring the heirs
of deceased decree-holder on record. The reason
which has been assigned by the petitioner in the Delay
Condonation Application was that he could not get the
details of the heirs of the deceased decree holder at
later stage, coupled with the fact that he was not well
as such he could not file the application within the time.
4. This reason assigned in the application under
Section 5, did not impressed the attention of the
learned Court below and consequently his application
under Section 5 was rejected by the impugned order
dated 07.09.2017, as a result of which the Substitution
Application too stood rejected.

3
5. Though Article 123 of the Limitation Act
contemplates filing of an application from the date of
the knowledge, which in the instant case, as far as the
petitioner is concerned, would be attributed to be from
11.02.2016 when respondents filed abatement
application. But looking to the language used by
legislature for the purposes of considering the
conodation of delay in a proceeding it has been laid
down that there has to be sufficient cause. There are
catena of judgments, which lay down that sufficient
cause does not mean a good cause. It should be a
cause enough to meet the ends of justice for enabling
the parties to the lis to have an adjudication of their
case on its own merits instead of the technicalities of
the limitation and substitution.
6. This Court, too, though hesitatingly is
permitting the petitioner to bring the heirs of the
deceased decree holder on record just solely for the
purposes that the lis between the parties may be
decided on merits. As such the writ petition is allowed.
The impugned order, rejecting the Delay Condonation
Application consequently the Substitution Application is
quashed. The substitution as well as the delay
condonation application is allowed, subject to the cost
of payment of Rs. 20,000/- to be paid by the petitioner
to the heirs of the decree holder.

4
7. Furthermore, since the proceedings are
pending for a considerable long time, it is hoped and
trusted that the Additional District Judge, Haridwar who
is ceased with an Appeal No. 75 of 2015 will decide the
appeal itself within the period of 6 months from today
without granting any unnecessary adjournments to the
petitioner.
8. Subject to the above condition, the writ
petition is allowed. No order as to cost.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
02.11.2017
Mahinder/
